title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-21
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 6NT. West's lead is won by East with the ♠A. East returns the suit, won by South. South must hope to play the diamond suit for 4 tricks. It is necessary to assume that East has the ♦K.

If East has a singleton ♦K, South must begin the suit by cashing the ♦A. South can then finesse against West's ♦10.

If East has a doubleton ♦K, South must cross to dummy and lead a diamond honour. If East covers, South wins and can finesse against the ♦10 with West. If East ducks the first diamond lead, the ♦A will drop the ♦K on the next round.

If East has 3 diamonds to the ♦K, it is necessary to assume that West has the ♦10. East cannot gain by covering the first diamond play from dummy. Dummy's other diamond honour is then played, pinning the ♦10 in West's hand.

In order to find out how to play the diamonds, it is best to cash the other suits first (making sure to end in dummy). Three rounds of hearts show that East started with 5 hearts. A third round of spades reveals that East began with 2 spades. Finally, 3 rounds of clubs complete the count. East also began with 5 clubs and there is room for only 1 diamond in his hand. South must assume it is the ♦K and lead low to his ♦A.

If the count of the hand is not perfect, South will have to guess how many diamonds East started with.
